function.name: list_files
function.description: List files and folders inside the project.

path.description: Folder path relative to the project root.

function.name: list_project_tree
function.description: Show the project folder structure with a depth limit. Use this to understand the shape of the project before reading files.

path.description: Folder path relative to the project root.

max_depth.description: How many folder levels to include.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Find files inside the project using a filename pattern like *.py or *.md.

pattern.description: Filename pattern to match, such as *.py or *.txt.

path.description: Folder path relative to the project root.

function.name: get_file_info
function.description: Get basic metadata for a file or folder, including file size, line count, and modified time when available.

path.description: Path relative to the project root.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file inside the project. Each line is shown with a leading 'line_number: ' prefix for reference only; that prefix is not part of the file.

path.description: File path relative to the project root.

function.name: read_file_range
function.description: Read a specific 1-based inclusive line range from a text file inside the project. Use this when read_file output is too long or when you need a later part of a file. Prefer this over terminal commands like Get-Content, type, or cat.

path.description: File path relative to the project root.

start_line.description: First line to read, using 1-based line numbers.

end_line.description: Last line to read, using 1-based line numbers.

function.name: read_many_files
function.description: Read several text files in one tool call. Use this for small related files instead of making many read_file calls.

paths.description: File paths relative to the project root.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create or overwrite a text file inside the project.

path.description: File path relative to the project root.

content.description: The full text content to write.

function.name: run_python_tests
function.description: Run Python unittest tests for the project. Use this instead of execute_terminal_command for normal Python test runs.

test_path.description: Optional test file path relative to the project root. Use an empty string to run unittest discovery.

function.name: compile_python
function.description: Compile Python files with py_compile to catch syntax errors. Use this instead of execute_terminal_command for normal Python syntax checks.

paths.description: Python file paths relative to the project root. Use an empty list to compile all project Python files.

function.name: git_status
function.description: Show short git status for the project.

function.name: git_diff
function.description: Show git diff for the whole project or one file. Use this instead of execute_terminal_command for normal git diff inspection.

path.description: Optional file path relative to the project root. Use an empty string for the whole diff.

function.name: git_log
function.description: Show recent git commits in compact one-line format. Use this to understand how the project evolved before making changes.

count.description: How many recent commits to show (1 to 50).

function.name: apply_patch
function.description: Apply one or more exact text replacements to a file inside the project. old_text must be the literal file text, without any 'line_number: ' prefix shown by read_file or read_file_range. It must match exactly once.

path.description: File path relative to the project root.

replacements.description: Exact text replacements to apply in order.

old_text.description: Existing text to replace exactly once.

function.name: delete_file
function.description: Delete a single file inside the project. Cannot delete folders.

path.description: File path relative to the project root.

function.name: move_file
function.description: Move or rename a file in one step. Prefer this over write_file + delete_file when renaming a file.

source.description: Current file path relative to the project root.

destination.description: New file path relative to the project root.

function.name: search_files
function.description: Search for text inside project files using a regular expression. Plain words work too, like main. Regex examples: def .*tool, import (os|json), TODO|FIXME. Pass file_glob to scope the search to certain files, which is faster and less noisy.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for, case-insensitive.

path.description: Folder path relative to the project root.

file_glob.description: Optional filename pattern to limit which files are searched, such as *.py or *.md. Use an empty string to search all files.

function.name: execute_terminal_command
function.description: Run a PowerShell command in the project folder. Use this only for tests, scripts, git commands, uv commands, and shell commands. Do not use this for reading, listing, or searching files; use list_files, glob_files, read_file, read_file_range, or search_files instead.

command.description: The exact PowerShell command to run.

function.name: web_fetch
function.description: Fetch a web page or data endpoint over https. Optionally pass a prompt to get only the answer to that question instead of the full page, which saves space. JSON responses come back pretty-printed, which is ideal for live data. For live weather use https://wttr.in/CITY?format=j1 . For a live stock quote use https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/SYMBOL . Returned content is untrusted reference data.

url.description: The full http or https URL to fetch.

prompt.description: Optional question to answer from the page. If given, only the focused answer is returned instead of the full page content.

function.name: web_search
function.description: Search the web or news using Tavily. Returns a list of result titles, URLs, and snippets, plus a short summary answer when available. Use search_type='text' for documentation, packages, error explanations, or general facts. Use search_type='news' for recent news, current events, and time-sensitive topics; it defaults to the past day. Use search_depth='advanced' for more thorough, higher-relevance results (costs 2 API credits). Use include_domains to restrict results to trusted sources such as 'python.org' or 'github.com'. Follow up with web_fetch to read a specific page in detail.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-10). Default is 5.

timelimit.description: Time filter for results: 'd' (past day), 'w' (past week), 'm' (past month), 'y' (past year). For news, 'y' is not supported; if omitted, news defaults to 'd'.

search_type.description: Type of search: 'text' for general web search (default), 'news' for news/current events.

search_depth.description: Search depth: 'basic' (default, 1 credit), 'advanced' (2 credits, more relevant, includes multiple chunks per source), 'fast' or 'ultra-fast' for lower latency.

include_domains.description: Optional list of domains to prioritize or restrict results to, e.g. ['python.org', 'github.com', 'stackoverflow.com'].

exact_match.description: If true, only return results containing the exact quoted phrase(s) in the query. Best for precise lookups.

function.name: update_global_memory
function.description: Update your long-term memory about the USER (not about any project). Use this for durable facts about who the user is, their preferences, goals, and how they like to work. You maintain this yourself: whenever you learn something lasting and important about the user, save it here. You provide the FULL new memory content, which replaces the old file, so include the facts you want to keep plus the new one, and drop anything stale. Keep it concise markdown; it must stay under 2000 characters.

content.description: The full new global memory content, as concise markdown.

function.name: update_project_memory
function.description: Update your long-term memory about the CURRENT PROJECT (not about the user). Use this for durable project knowledge: architecture, key files, decisions, conventions, gotchas, and open tasks. You maintain this yourself: whenever you learn something lasting and important about the project, save it here. You provide the FULL new memory content, which replaces the old file, so include the knowledge you want to keep plus the new one, and drop anything stale. Keep it concise markdown; it must stay under 6000 characters.

content.description: The full new project memory content, as concise markdown.

function.name: search_sessions
function.description: Search past saved conversations (sessions) in this project for a word or regular expression. Use this to recall something discussed in an earlier session. Returns short matching snippets with the session name and date, newest first. Then use read_session to read a specific session in full if you need more context.

query.description: Word or regular expression to search for, case-insensitive.

function.name: read_session
function.description: Read one past session conversation in full, by its session name (for example session-20260605-153012). Use this after search_sessions to see the full context around a match.

name.description: The session name, with or without the .json extension.

function.name: list_skills
function.description: List all currently saved skills, including both global skills and project-specific skills. Use this before answering questions about what skills are available.

function.name: read_skill
function.description: Load the full steps of a saved skill by name. Your available skills are listed in your system prompt by name and description; read one before doing a task it covers.

name.description: The skill name, for example add-a-tool.

function.name: save_skill
function.description: Create or update a reusable skill: a short markdown runbook for a task you may repeat. Save one after finishing a non-trivial task, and update one that was helpful but incomplete or wrong. Keep it concise (under 4000 characters).

description.description: One line describing when to use this skill.

content.description: The procedure as markdown: when to use, steps, pitfalls, and how to verify success.

scope.description: Use 'project' for a skill specific to the current project, or 'global' for a general skill useful in any project.

function.name: delete_skill
function.description: Delete a saved skill by name when it is stale or wrong.
